title: Benchmark Proof Points - Slides Inputs
content:
WORKING SHEET (slides inputs) — Benchmark Proof Points + acceptable ranges
Last reviewed: 2025-02-05 (PMM + Platform + SRE)
Owner: Soojin Lee

Purpose
- Provide slide-safe, verbally-safe benchmark statements for Standard Demo v1.
- We do NOT show hard numbers on slides unless explicitly approved. Default is ranges + conditions.
- Any claim must be anchored to: (a) demo tenant dashboards (b) internal load test notes (c) “what the prospect will experience” in the live demo.

How to use
- For the deck: use only rows where “Slide-safe?” = YES.
- For live talk track: ranges are OK; always qualify with the “Conditions / caveats” column.
- If asked for exact numbers: offer to run a prospect-specific benchmark during eval (don’t improvise).

Definitions (for consistency)
- TTFT = time-to-first-token (streaming) measured client-side.
- E2E latency = total time to full completion (non-streaming) for the given output length.
- Throughput = sustained output tokens/second at steady state under batching.
- Cost metrics are directional (relative) unless Finance-approved. Avoid $ on slides; use “% lower / higher” or “unit cost improvements”.

APPROVAL / GUARDRAILS
- Marketing (Camila) guidance: no absolute $/1M token on slides; ranges allowed verbally if labeled as “typical internal tests” and paired with conditions.
- SRE (Sean) guidance: avoid quoting p95 from a single run; use “typical” + “p95 target” language.
- Platform (Logan/Chloe) guidance: only cite metrics we can show in Console dashboards live (demo tenant dashboards).

================================================================================
TABLE: CLAIMS + SAFE RANGES
(Format: one row per claim)

Columns:
ID | Persona | Deployment mode | Workload | Claim (slide wording) | Talk-track wording (verbatim-safe) | Metric(s) | Acceptable range (what to say) | Conditions / caveats | Source / how to validate | Slide mapping | Slide-safe? | Reviewer notes / TODO

BP-01 | Platform Eng | Hosted + Dedicated | Streaming chat | “Fast time-to-first-token with streaming” | “On typical chat prompts, you’ll see first token in well under a second. The key is you can watch it live, and we break down where the time goes.” | TTFT (p50/p95) | p50: 150–500ms; p95: 400–900ms | Model + region dependent. TTFT can spike on cold start or after pinned version change. Always demo from seeded prompt first. | Demo tenant dashboard: Latency → TTFT panel; Scenario script: streaming_chat.py; Validate during pre-demo checklist | Deck: Performance section; Talk track: Scenario 1 | YES | Keep “well under a second” on slide, ranges only verbally.

BP-02 | ML Eng | Hosted | Short-form generation | “High throughput under load via batching” | “When traffic increases, the runtime batches efficiently so you get better GPU utilization without blowing up latency.” | Throughput (tok/s) + E2E latency | Throughput improvement vs unbatched: 1.5×–3×; E2E latency increase: typically <20% at moderate concurrency | Requires batching enabled + compatible request mix. If asked: show Console → Optimize suggestion + batch settings. | Demo tenant dashboard: Throughput panel; Internal load test notes (SE dry runs); Console route config (batching) | Deck: Cost/Performance controls | YES | Never claim a fixed tok/s number publicly.

BP-03 | Platform Eng | Dedicated | Mixed chat traffic | “Predictable latency with reserved capacity” | “With Dedicated, we reserve GPUs for your tenant, so you’re not competing with other customers. That shows up as steadier p95s at the same load.” | p95 TTFT + p95 E2E | p95 variance reduction: typically 30%–60% lower jitter vs multi-tenant; p95 TTFT stays <1s for demo workload | Must qualify: depends on chosen capacity and target concurrency. We can size to an SLO; demo shows the concept, not a guarantee. | Dedicated demo tenant (if enabled) + dashboard comparison view; SRE runbook notes on alert thresholds | Deck: Dedicated value slide | YES | Phrase carefully: “steadier” not “guaranteed”.

BP-04 | Security | Private (VPC) | Regulated deployment | “Same performance tooling in private deployments” | “The point isn’t only private networking—your operators still get the same observability and rollout controls to keep latency and cost predictable.” | Feature parity proof (dashboards/rollouts) | N/A (qualitative) | Keep it qualitative. If asked about absolute perf: offer to benchmark in customer VPC/on-prem context. | Console screenshots + Private architecture diagram references; Demo talk track branch | YES | Don’t imply identical perf across all hardware.

BP-05 | Platform Eng | Hosted + Dedicated | Reliability/fallback | “Graceful degradation with fallback routing” | “If a route hits errors or capacity issues, we can automatically fail over to a compatible model variant or region based on policy—without your app changing.” | Error rate + failover time | Demonstrate failover within 1–5s; 5xx reduced during incident by routing | Only demo with controlled fault injection (toggle route to ‘simulate capacity constrained’). Avoid claiming ‘zero downtime’. | Demo scenario: fallback_routing.md; Console route policy view; Dashboard: Errors + Route changes | Deck: Reliability section | YES | Make sure demo toggle is still present in Console build.

BP-06 | Procurement / Finance | Hosted | Unit economics | “Lower unit cost via caching + routing policies” | “Across many workloads, teams see double-digit % improvements when they enable caching and choose a cost-aware route policy. We’ll quantify it on your traffic during eval.” | Relative cost per request / per token | Typical improvement: 15%–45% lower cost on repeated-prefix traffic; 10%–25% lower on mixed traffic with routing | Only holds when there is prefix repetition and cache hit rate >~20%. Avoid $ claims. | Demo tenant: Cost dashboard (token cost breakdown); Scenario: prefix_cache_demo; Validate with before/after saved view | Deck: Optimize section | YES | Safe to say “double-digit percent” on slide; ranges verbally.

BP-07 | ML Eng | Hosted | Structured output | “Better reliability for structured outputs” | “When you need JSON back, we support structured output modes so you’re not just hoping the model behaves.” | JSON validity rate | Qualitative: “materially reduces parsing failures”; If pressed: 60%–90%+ improvement vs baseline prompt-only on demo task | Avoid quoting exact % unless we run the exact same prompt/test in-session. Keep to ‘reduces failures’. | Demo scenario script: structured_output.py; Console error analysis for parse failures | Deck: Developer experience / quality | YES | Ensure we have a fallback story if model returns invalid JSON live.

BP-08 | Platform Eng | Hosted | Tail latency | “Observability to diagnose p95/p99 regressions” | “We show latency percentiles by route and model version, so if p95 creeps up you can see whether it’s queueing, compute, or downstream.” | Console panels (queueing vs compute) | N/A (qualitative) | Don’t claim root-cause accuracy beyond what telemetry supports. | Demo tenant dashboards: Latency breakdown panel; Saved view ‘Latency regression drilldown’ | Deck: Console/observability | YES | Screenshot must match current Console nav.

BP-09 | Platform Eng | Dedicated + Private | Rollouts | “Safe rollouts with canary + auto fallback” | “You can canary a new model/quant profile to 5% traffic, watch errors/latency, then auto-roll back if thresholds trip.” | Rollback trigger time | Typical rollback execution: <2 minutes after threshold breach (demo) | Demo uses synthetic threshold; real rollback depends on monitoring interval + config. | Console: Rollouts screen; Demo scenario: canary_rollout.md | Deck: Operations section | YES | Avoid claiming “automatic” unless we show it live.

BP-10 | ML Eng | Hosted | Embeddings | “Fast embeddings for retrieval workloads” | “For embeddings, latency is typically tens of milliseconds for small batches, and throughput scales with batch size.” | Embedding latency | p50: 20–80ms (small batch); p95: 40–150ms | Strongly hardware/model dependent; region matters. Only talk ranges. | Demo endpoint script: embeddings_demo; Dashboard: Embeddings latency panel | Deck: API surface slide (optional appendix) | YES | If this slide is cut, keep for Q&A.

BP-11 | Platform Eng | Hosted | Rate limits / quotas | “Predictable throttling + clear signals” | “If you hit a quota, you get consistent 429s with clear headers—so your client can backoff predictably.” | 429 behavior + headers | Qualitative; show headers live | Must ensure demo tenant quotas are set to avoid accidental throttling during primary path; show throttling only in optional branch. | Demo tenant config; Support ticket learnings; Talk track sidebar | YES | Confirm headers in SDK snippet match current gateway.

BP-12 | Any | Hosted + Dedicated + Private | Cross-env consistency | “Same API + same config primitives across environments” | “The API surface and core controls—routing, versions, dashboards—stay consistent whether you run hosted, dedicated, or in your VPC.” | Qualitative | N/A | Don’t overclaim 100% parity; use “same primitives / consistent experience.” | Product docs + Console screenshots; PRD demo environment | YES | Make sure we have one slide showing the 3 deployment modes.

================================================================================
“DO NOT SAY” LIST (until re-approved)
- Any absolute “$X per 1M tokens” or “$X/hr” numbers (deck or verbal).
- “Guaranteed p95 < ___ ms” without a signed SLA context.
- “Zero downtime” / “never drops requests” claims.
- Fixed tokens/sec numbers without specifying hardware + model + sequence lengths.
- “SOC2 certified” unless Legal has approved the exact phrasing for the current audit period (use: “SOC 2 Type II available under NDA” if current).

================================================================================
NOTES / OPEN ITEMS
- TODO (Logan/Chloe): confirm demo tenant dashboards include TTFT and queueing breakdown panels after latest observability-pack import.
- TODO (Soojin): align slide wording to remove ‘p99’ references (we don’t show p99 in Console by default in demo).
- TODO (Camila): confirm final approved wording for “double-digit % cost improvements” (OK) vs “up to 50%” (too aggressive).
- TODO (Sean): confirm acceptable verbal framing for failover timing (1–5s) based on current routing policy implementation.

Change log
- 2025-02-05: tightened TTFT p95 verbal range; removed absolute tok/s values; added “DO NOT SAY” list.
- 2025-01-22: initial table created from dry run notes + demo tenant dashboards.
